question.text: Paragraph: Let $p$ be an odd prime number and $T_p$ be the following set of $2 \times 2$ matrices $$ T_p=\left\{A=\left[\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ c & a \end{array}\right] ; a, b, c \in\{0,1,2, \ldots, p-1\}\right\} $$Question: The number of $A$ in $T_p$ such that the trace of $A$ is not divisible by $p$ but det $(A)$ is divisible by $p$ is [Note : The trace of a matrix is the sum of its diagonal entries.]

solution.text:
Trace of $A=2 a$, will be divisible by $p$ iff $a=0$.
$|A|=a^2-b c$, for $\left(a^2-b c\right)$ to be divisible
by $p$. There are exactly $(p-1)$ ordered pairs $(b, c)$ for any value of $a$.
$\therefore$ Required number is $(p-1)^2$.
Hence, (c) is the correct option.
